name: Perfume Genius
label: Matador
lede: A kid who dropped out of a Seattle high school, posted piano songs to Myspace, and ended up on Letterman, in a Grammy nomination and in a dance theater with a saxophone and a string section.

eras.title: From a Seattle bedroom to Myspace
eras.text: Mike Hadreas grew up outside Seattle, left, came back, and started writing piano songs at home. He put them online under a name borrowed from a movie.

years.h: Mike Hadreas is born in Des Moines, Iowa
years.p: He moves to the Seattle suburbs at about six or seven; he studies painting and takes piano lessons.
years.xp: Wikipedia gives his birth as September 25, 1981 and says he moved to the Seattle suburbs when he was six or seven. His mother worked as a special education teacher and later as an assistant principal.

years.h: Back in Seattle after a bad stretch in New York
years.p: Hadreas works as a doorman at an East Village club, returns to Seattle in 2005 and starts recording at home.
years.xp:
Wikipedia reports he dropped out of high school in his senior year after threats the administration ignored, and was attacked by several young men two years later. He then moved to Williamsburg, Brooklyn.

The Fader adds that he partied hard in New York and returned home to a 20-day rehab. The songs that became Learning started after that, recorded at his mother's house.

years.h: Myspace page goes up under the name Perfume Genius
years.p: The name comes from the protagonist of Tom Tykwer's 2006 film Perfume: The Story of a Murderer.

eras.title: Matador and the piano that wouldn't stay quiet
eras.text: Learning arrives on Matador. Hadreas meets the pianist who becomes his partner and collaborator, then makes a second record that YouTube flags.

years.h: Mike Hadreas meets Alan Wyffels
years.p: A mutual friend introduces them; Wyffels, a classically trained pianist, becomes his touring pianist and later his partner.
years.xp: The Fader says the friend hoped Wyffels could help Hadreas get sober, and that Wyffels took him to AA meetings. Wikipedia says they began dating soon after. Wyffels co-wrote Glory and plays on the later records.

years.h: Learning: bedroom songs on Matador
years.p: Matador puts it out in the US, Turnstile in Europe. Pitchfork gave it 8.2.
years.xp:
Many of the songs were recorded at home. Wikipedia credits the Myspace page for the attention that led to the release.

His first live show was at the Vera Project in Seattle, opening for A Sunny Day in Glasgow, with Wyffels on piano for the tour that followed.

years.h: Put Your Back N 2 It and the video YouTube flagged
years.p: The promo video has Hadreas embracing adult performer Arpad Miklos; YouTube marked it unsuitable for family audiences.
years.xp: The record drew a second round of praise. Wikipedia reports the YouTube flag.

years.h: Hadreas sings on Cate Le Bon's Mug Museum
years.p: He takes guest vocals on "I Think I Knew", the first of many collaborations outside his own records.

eras.title: Too Bright: loud, weird and in charge
eras.text: A record that puts a bigger sound and a sharper persona on the same page, then a TV spot that puts it in front of a late-night audience.

years.cap: Too Bright (2014), artwork by Luke Gilford
years.h: Too Bright: Portishead's Adrian Utley co-produces
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.5 and Best New Music; Metacritic lists it at 87.
years.xp:
Adrian Utley of [[Portishead|8f6bd1e4-fbe1-4f50-aa9b-94c450ec0f11]] and Ali Chant co-produced. The album reached No. 83 on the US Billboard 200 and No. 77 in the UK, per Wikipedia.

"Queen" and "Grid" went on to turn up in TV series including Mr. Robot and The Great.

years.h: Hadreas plays "Queen" on The Late Show with David Letterman
years.p: His late-night TV debut, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Sharon Van Etten joins him on a Grateful Dead cover
years.p: "To Lay Me Down" appears on Day of the Dead, a benefit tribute for the Red Hot Organization, released May 20, 2016.

years.h: Prada uses his Elvis cover in fragrance ads
years.p: "Can't Help Falling in Love" runs in campaigns for La Femme and L'Homme, per Wikipedia.

eras.title: Blake Mills and the big pop record
eras.text: With producer Blake Mills, Hadreas makes two albums that Pitchfork scores 8.8 and 9.0, and starts to curate and collaborate as well as write.

years.h: "Slip Away" arrives, directed by Björk's video collaborator
years.p: Andrew Thomas Huang, who has worked with [[Björk|87c5dedd-371d-4a53-9f7f-80522fb7f3cb]], directs it; Pitchfork tags it Best New Track.

years.h: No Shape goes to Pitchfork as Best New Music
years.p: Recorded October to December 2016 in Los Angeles with Blake Mills; Pitchfork gave it 8.8.
years.xp:
Shawn Everett mixed it. The album was nominated at the 60th Grammys for Best Engineered Album, Non-Classical, and Pitchfork later ranked it No. 70 on its 200 best albums of the 2010s, according to Wikipedia.

The Fader put him on its March/April cover that year; in that story he spoke about his sobriety and about living with Crohn's disease since childhood.

years.h: Hadreas curates Le Guess Who? in Utrecht
years.p: He picks Aldous Harding, Mount Eerie, Weyes Blood and Le Mystère des Voix Bulgares.

years.h: "Otherside" plays in the trailer for The Goldfinch
years.p: The film adapts Donna Tartt's novel.

years.src: Wikipedia: Set My Heart on Fire Immediately
years.h: Set My Heart on Fire Immediately: Sound City, Pino Palladino
years.p: Recorded at Sound City in Van Nuys with Blake Mills; Pitchfork scored it 9.0 and ranked it No. 5 of 2020.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists bassist Pino Palladino, drummer Matt Chamberlain, violinist Rob Moose and Phoebe Bridgers on harmony vocals. Hadreas named Townes Van Zandt, Enya and the Cocteau Twins among his influences. Metacritic has it at 91, his highest.

eras.title: Ugly Season: a dance piece becomes a record
eras.text: The pandemic pushes Hadreas toward a stage project. He scores a dance with Kate Wallich, then decides the music should stand on its own.

years.h: Kate Wallich and Hadreas start The Sun Still Burns Here
years.p: Hadreas wrote the score for the Seattle choreographer's piece, with Alan Wyffels improvising on it.
years.xp:
Hadreas told Document Journal the project started because he and Wallich decided to make a dance performance together. He added that he'd never made anything where someone else was involved from the very beginning.

Mills produced, and the music was always meant to exist on its own, too.

q: It can be an album, a dance piece, a short film, all of it.
years.h: Ugly Season: Pitchfork gives it 8.6, ranks it No. 26 of 2022
years.p: Ten tracks, 52 minutes, on Matador. Metacritic's average across 18 critics is 79.
years.xp:
Wikipedia credits Blake Mills with production and lists saxophonist Sam Gendel, string arranger Rob Moose and drummer Matt Chamberlain. Paste gave it 8.4 and put it at No. 23 on its year-end list. It reached No. 39 on the UK Independent Albums chart.

Hadreas told Billboard the record could be an album, a dance piece or a short film; artist Jacolby Satterwhite directed that film, Pygmalion's Ugly Season.

years.h: Back on the road after the pandemic
years.p: Hadreas told Billboard from Sydney that he enjoys live performing "way more than I ever have".
years.xp: Billboard spoke to him from Sydney, after the New Zealand dates.

eras.title: Glory, and a wedding
eras.text: Hadreas covers a standard for a TV show, then returns with another Blake Mills record that Wyffels co-wrote.

years.h: He covers "What a Diff'rence a Day Makes" for The New Look
years.p: Jack Antonoff produces the take for the Apple TV series.

years.h: Glory: Blake Mills, Alan Wyffels and Aldous Harding
years.p: Announced January 15 with "It's a Mirror", which Pitchfork tagged Best New Track.
years.xp: Wikipedia also lists Jim Keltner, Meg Duffy and Gregory Uhlmann. Hadreas and Wyffels married in 2025, per the same article.
